title: Four-tier quant profiling cheatsheet and sample calcs
body:
Purpose and quick summary:
This is a compact working sheet + reference for profiling models across four quant tiers we use in experiments: 32-bit baseline, FP8-ish (8-bit float or block-fp8), INT8 (symmetric/asymmetric per-channel), and 4-bit (GPTQ / AWQ style). Goal: fast heuristics to convert a latency+cost SLO into a recommended quant tier and light pre-deployment checklist.

Intended audience:
- ML infra / product engineers running pre-serve perf runs
- Solutions engineers advising customers on cost-latency tradeoffs
- Product PMs who need a one-pager for canary config suggestions

High-level decision flow (one-line each):
1) Capture SLO: p95 latency budget per request, plus monthly token budget (tokens/month).
2) Measure baseline 32-bit QPS and p95 for representative prompt distribution.
3) Measure each candidate quant tier on same hardware (same batch sizes / prompt length distribution).
4) Compute cost-per-token for each tier = (instance hourly $ / tokens served per hour) adjusted for GPU utilization.
5) Score tiers by multi-objective metric (latency penalty + quality delta + cost saving). Pick tier with acceptable quality delta under threshold.

Key knobs and shorthand definitions (for the sheet columns):
- model_name: e.g., gpt-small-v1
- hw: e.g., A100-80GB, H100-80GB, L4-40GB
- quant_tier: baseline_fp32, fp8, int8, 4bit
- p95_ms: measured p95 in milliseconds at target real-world concurrency
- tokens_per_sec: sustained throughput under typical batching strategy
- inst_hr_cost: instance hourly cost (cloud list price or committed rate)
- tokens_per_hr = tokens_per_sec * 3600
- $/token = inst_hr_cost / tokens_per_hr (adjust for multi-tenancy overhead as needed)
- quality_metric_delta: e.g., delta in eval accuracy/ROUGE/LLM-eval score relative to baseline (positive means worse)
- accept_quality_thresh: default 1.5% relative delta or +/- 0.02 absolute (tunable per customer)

Concrete sample rows (toy numbers) - copy into sheet to start: 
- Baseline fp32 on A100-80GB: p95_ms=210, tokens_per_sec=5200, inst_hr_cost=$9.6 -> tokens_per_hr=18,720,000 -> $/token=5.12e-7
- FP8 on A100: p95_ms=185, tokens_per_sec=5600, inst_hr_cost=$9.6 -> tokens_per_hr=20,160,000 -> $/token=4.76e-7, quality_delta=+0.6%
- INT8 on A100: p95_ms=160, tokens_per_sec=6000, inst_hr_cost=$9.6 -> tokens_per_hr=21,600,000 -> $/token=4.44e-7, quality_delta=+1.1%
- 4-bit on A100: p95_ms=145, tokens_per_sec=6500, inst_hr_cost=$9.6 -> tokens_per_hr=23,400,000 -> $/token=4.10e-7, quality_delta=+2.9%

Recommendation scoring formula (quick heuristic used in sheet):
score = normalized_cost_saving * 0.5 + normalized_latency_gain * 0.3 - normalized_quality_penalty * 0.8
Where normalized_* are scaled to [0,1] across the candidate tiers for the run. We weight quality penalty more heavily by default. Tune weights per-customer SLOs.

SLO-aware decision rules (practical shortcuts):
- If p95_measured <= 0.8 * p95_budget then prefer lower-bit tier with +quality monitoring; use canary split 5-10% traffic.
- If p95_measured > p95_budget -> avoid further quant steps that give <5% latency improvement; prefer model sharding or smaller sequence-length heuristics first.
- If tokens/month cost saving < 1% -> skip quant rollout (operational overhead not worth it).

Quality validation checklist (pre-canary):
- Run 3 prompt suites: safety-ish, business critical prompts, long-context prompts. Collect token-level logprobs and failure modes.
- Collect regression alerts: exact match, BLEU/ROUGE, hallucination rate proxies, and a small human review of 200 samples for the chosen tier.
- Add fallback policy: if model output score (LLM-eval aggregated) drops > accept_quality_thresh on live traffic, route to baseline until triage.

Batching and cache notes (how they shift numbers):
- Effective tokens/sec scales with batch size until memory-bound; each quant tier changes memory footprint -> allows larger batch -> non-linear throughput gains for INT8/4-bit.
- KV cache size is smaller for int8/4-bit, lowering memory pressure and improving concurrent QPS. Include cache hit-rate assumptions in tokens_per_sec col.

Edge-case heuristics we use in experiments: 
- For short prompts (<64 tokens) latency wins; give heavier weight to p95 differences and prefer INT8 over 4-bit because quant noise matters more for short-span completions.
- For long generation tasks (>512 tokens), throughput and memory footprint dominate; 4-bit usually gives best $/token but watch for drift in score.
- Mixed workloads: split by percentile of prompt length and compute weighted score per quant tier.

Notes on hardware interaction (practical):
- H100: FP8 execution paths are often more optimized than INT8; FP8 p95 delta vs fp32 may be smaller. Always measure fp8 separately.
- A100: INT8 commonly has large kernel speedups; AWQ/LLM.int4 variants depend on fused-kernel support.
- Cloud GPUs have different pricing models (spot / sustained use discounts) — attach the committed rate in inst_hr_cost when estimating production.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Add column for retry/backoff cost (percent extra tokens due to retries) — we sometimes see 1.5x effective tokens for noisy LLM interactions.
- Automate trimming of eval prompt set to be representative of customer's tail latencies.
- Add small Monte Carlo sim to estimate probability of quality regression exceeding threshold under data drift.

Rollout play for recommended tier (example):
1) Internal staging run with 10k prompts from production shadow for 24hrs. Confirm quality delta <= 1x accept threshold.
2) Canary 5% traffic, 2x monitoring frequency (per-minute evaluation for first 6 hrs).
3) If stable, increase to 25% after 24hrs, then 100% after 72hrs.
4) If any quality alert triggers, automatic rollback to baseline variant and create incident.

Appendix: quick calc snippets to paste into a spreadsheet (text formulas)
- tokens_per_hr = tokens_per_sec * 3600
- $per_token = inst_hr_cost / tokens_per_hr
- monthly_cost = $per_token * monthly_tokens_expected
- relative_cost_saving = (baseline_monthly_cost - tier_monthly_cost) / baseline_monthly_cost

Rough example customer scenario (for marketing/sales):
- 50M tokens / month, p95_budget = 300 ms on H100 cluster. Baseline fp32 monthly = $X. INT8 gives 18% cost reduction and p95=240ms -> recommended: INT8 canary, monitor for quality delta; projected $ saved = $Y/month.

Contact and provenance:
- Author: Aisha Kumar (product-optimize)
- Experiments and sample numbers pulled from internal perf runs Feb 2025 with H100 and A100 dev clusters.
- Reach out to Mateo (bench infra) for raw perf traces and Priya for eval suite details.

Notes-to-self / scratch: 
- Might fold this into the interactive cost-model worksheet that calculates expected monthly savings given arbitrary concurrency mix and retention TTL for KV caches.
- Keep a library of canonical prompt sets for short/medium/long to speed A/B analysis.

End of cheatsheet (working).
